reason: H0 never calls the S1 production API meshopt_filterIndexBuffer. The API processes attacker-variable index topology and vertex byte data through remapping and triangle hashing, with behavior depending on vertex_count, vertex_size, and vertex_stride. Existing harnesses exercise meshlet building, codecs, and simplification, but do not cover filtering of position-equivalent degenerates or winding-sensitive duplicate triangles.
evidence: meshopt_filterIndexBuffer is introduced at src/indexgenerator.cpp:426 and is absent from every H0 call site.
The function passes indices, index_count, vertex_count, and a VertexHasher configured by vertex_size and vertex_stride into generateVertexRemap.
It removes triangles when remapped vertices satisfy ra == rb, ra == rc, or rb == rc.
It canonicalizes cyclic rotations before using TriangleKeyHasher and hashLookup, while the declaration explicitly preserves duplicates with opposite windings.

H0's tools/clusterfuzz.cpp fixes vertices to 100 float[4] records and targets meshopt_buildMeshlets*, meshopt_partitionClusters; tools/codecfuzz.cpp targets codec APIs; tools/simplifyfuzz.cpp targets meshopt_simplify* APIs.
recommended_action: Add a dedicated fuzz target for meshopt_filterIndexBuffer that derives valid index_count multiples of three, in-range indices, vertex_count, vertex_size in 1..256, and vertex_stride >= vertex_size from fuzz data. Vary arbitrary vertex bytes and repeated positions; generate degenerate, cyclically rotated duplicate, opposite-winding, hash-collision, empty, and highly duplicated triangle sets. Check output bounds and triangle alignment, retained-index validity, removal semantics, opposite-winding preservation, determinism, and safe in-place operation if that usage is supported.
